transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands — April 10 2026
Start: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~62 minutes | Host: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya Chen (CEO), Jordan Lee (CTO), Priya Patel (VP Product), Ethan Rogers (Head of Sales), Samir Gupta (Head of Research), Alex Torres (Head of Reliability), plus all teams

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know it's a busy week so we appreciate it. Quick agenda: Q1 recap, product roadmap, infra and reliability, security update, hiring org, then Q&A.
[00:25] Maya: Quick headline — phenomenal start to the year. Usage week over week is up ~48% quarter-over-quarter, and we're pacing well against our ARR targets. Not to overclaim, but the Dedicated pilot with three customers is looking strong, latency numbers are improving and customers are sending great feedback.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Yeah just to add — infra work in March paid off. We landed a few kernel optimizations that dropped p99 token latency on the 4k context tests by about 18%, which matters a lot for chat use cases. There are still tail spikes when we hit cold kv-cache misses, which Alex will cover.
[01:45] Priya Patel: From product — Dedicated GA timeline: still on track for late Q2 for the first wave. Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot continues, a couple of enterprises signed NDAs and we're doing network reviews. We also plan to expand the model catalog with two mid-size foundation models and a quantized LLM variant for cheaper inference.
[02:20] Ethan Rogers: Sales side — pipeline is healthy, a couple of deals moving from POC to commitment this quarter. We had some pricing questions around dedicated capacity vs hosted — the playbook update will clarify the math and recommended upsell motions.
[02:50] Samir Gupta: Research update — we shipped an eval harness to measure quality regressions across quantization profiles; early results show certain workloads are more robust to 4-bit quantization than others. We'll publish a short note. Spoiler: enterprise retrieval reranking still prefers higher precision.
[03:25] Alex Torres: Reliability — two incidents in March caused ~6 minutes of increased error rates for a subset of tenants. Root cause was an autoscaler race where bursting replaced warm inference pods with cold ones. We've implemented a short-term fix (buffering policy) and a longer-term plan to change our rollout strategy to avoid cache thrash. I'll be scheduling retros.
[04:00] Maya: Great, thanks. On security and compliance — CISO team reported SOC 2 readiness is progressing; external audit is scheduled for late May. KMS integrations are in final QA for the private deploys. Also, we now have audit log retention options for Dedicated customers, should help close some enterprise procurement tickets.
[04:40] Jordan: Quick technical note — function calling and streaming support has been updated in the hosted API; SDKs will follow in the next week. There may be a few small breaking changes in the python SDK, but we'll doc them.
[05:10] Audience (Question): hi — can you talk about model pinning and rollbacks?
[05:20] Priya: Sure — we support model pinning per-route so you can lock a route to a particular model version. For rollbacks, our rollout engine supports canary and automatic fallback; we plan to expose more granular rollout metrics in the console in Q3.
[05:55] [07:00] Maya: Hiring — we're adding 18 roles across Eng and Product, and expanding Solutions and Sales for Dedicated/Private customers. Interview rubrics are being updated to emphasize production inference experience. People Ops will share the hiring plan in #people. Please refer candidates internally.
[07:35] Ethan: On GTM — playbooks for Dedicated include a recommended benchmark suite we ask customers to run; it helps with sizing and expected cost curves. We also have a billing FAQ to clarify burst vs reserved capacity charges.
[08:05] [10:00] Jordan: Benchmarks — quick preview: our 8k-context throughput for the quantized 7B model is roughly 2.3x higher than the float baseline at similar latency targets; will post the full spreadsheet. Note these are internal microbenchmarks, not apples-to-apples with other vendors — but useful for sizing.
[10:45] Audience (Question): Is there a timeline for broader open-model support?
[11:00] Samir: We're onboarding more open models to the catalog; target is to add two community models per month. The vetting includes perf profile, safety checks, and recommended quant configs.
[11:35] [15:00] Alex: Reliability deep-dive — warm pools and KV cache hit rates are key. We're introducing a smarter prefix cache to reduce cold starts and plan to tune autoscaler thresholds based on real traffic shapes per-customer. Early tests show a 25% reduction in cold starts in synthetic workloads.
[12:10] Priya: Product priorities for Q2 — finish Dedicated GA, make Private deploys easier (network docs and templates), improve console rollout observability, and deliver cheaper quantized serving profiles. We also want to improve prompt-set driven quality monitors in Redwood Optimize.
[12:45] Maya: Finance quick note — burn is within plan, and we expect to reach the next milestone with Dedicated expansions; no changes to comp or hiring cadence for now. Big focus is on efficient growth.
[13:10] Audience (Question): Any changes to data retention or encryption for Dedicated customers?
[13:25] Jordan: No radical changes — customers can choose retention windows and we support envelope encryption with KMS/HSM for Private. We're also adding more granular audit log exports.
[13:50] [20:00] Ethan: Customer stories — a retail customer cut inference cost by 38% after moving to a quantized profile and enabling prefix cache; another customer reduced user-facing p99 latency by 22% after switching routing policy. We'll share anonymized case notes.
[14:30] Samir: On safety and filters — we're improving structured output safety checks and expanding tests for hallucination types in long contexts. Noting that quantization sometimes amplifies certain failure modes — we test for that.
[15:05] [30:00] Maya: Leadership notes — thanks to Eng for hitting the kernel optimization milestone, to Product for tight work with customers on Dedicated pilots, and to Sales for pipeline expansion. Reminder: leadership office hours next week, sign up if you want 1:1 time.
[16:00] Audience (Question): Will there be a public benchmark post?
[16:15] Jordan: Yes, an internal-friendly benchmark spreadsheet will be posted and we'll craft a short blog that highlights methodology; aim to publish the data for developers to do their own comparisons.
[16:40] Priya: Also, roadmap callouts — we're adding structured output templates and better function-calling ergonomics for SDKs. Expect SDK releases in the next two sprints.
[17:10] [40:00] Alex: Incident follow-ups — two action items: increase buffer sizes for burst autoscaling and add a canary gating step for pod restarts. We're pushing both to staging tomorrow.
[17:45] Maya: OK let's move to Q&A. Please post questions in chat if you can't unmute.
[18:05] Audience (Question): How do we balance open source model support vs support burden?
[18:20] Samir: We'll prioritize models based on usage signals and cost/quality tradeoffs. Also provide recommended quant and fallback models. Support will be tiered — hosted gets baseline support, Dedicated customers have an SLA with deeper engineering support.
[19:00] Audience (Question): Are we exploring partnerships for global regions?
[19:15] Ethan: Yes, cloud marketplace listings and select infra partners in APAC are in progress; some pilot customers will test region-local hosting next quarter.
[19:40] [50:00] Maya: Wrap-up — big push on Dedicated GA and Private pilots this quarter. Please look out for the exec summary and the benchmark links. Thanks team.
[20:10] End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (names and acronyms may be slightly off); timestamps are approximate and inserted roughly every 30-90 seconds to emulate Fireflies export. Shared artifacts: slides (link in #all-hands), benchmark spreadsheet (coming), Dedicated pilot notes (internal drive).
